name: Vanuatu
headline: Vanuatu: +3.7% growth in 2025, 0.7% inflation, debt 36% of GDP
sections: Vanuatu is a $1.3 billion economy (2025), the world's 200th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.7% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $4,525 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 4.0% of GDP (2024).

Consumer prices rose 0.7% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 6.7% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.1% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 11.3% (2025).
Gross government debt is 36% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 43% in 2020. The general government balance is +6.2% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is −6.0% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 73% of GDP (2024), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 44% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 71.7 years (2024). Population: 334 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
